planting.note: Fall planting lets this nearly ever-blooming China rose establish before its long flowering season begins.

directions: One of the oldest cultivated China roses, grown in China long before its introduction to Europe around 1752, Old Blush bears semi-double, clear pink blooms with a light, sweet fragrance in nearly continuous flushes from spring to frost. As one of the four original 'stud Chinas' behind modern repeat-blooming roses, it is historically significant and remains outstandingly heat tolerant and low-maintenance. Its compact, twiggy growth suits borders, informal hedges, or large containers.

planting.note: Plant in fall to establish this compact China rose before its long repeat-bloom season.

directions: Bred by Coquereau in France and introduced in 1832, this China rose bears cupped, double blooms in a rich, velvety crimson, sometimes called 'Agrippina' in old nursery trade. It stays compact and twiggy, blooms almost continuously, and tolerates intense summer heat with little complaint, making it a long-time staple of old Gulf Coast and Deep South gardens. Its modest size suits foreground plantings and low hedges.

planting.note: Fall planting suits this reliable, compact China rose ahead of its nearly year-round bloom cycle.

directions: Introduced in France around 1840, Hermosa is a compact China rose with clear, soft pink, cupped double blooms carried in small clusters nearly nonstop through the growing season. Its neat, rounded habit and dependable repeat bloom made it a favorite for hedging in old Southern dooryard gardens long before modern repeat-flowering shrub roses existed. It is notably tolerant of heat, humidity, and poor soil.
